business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Bi-jural: Common Law for federal public and criminal law; Civil Law for Quebec private and commercial matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA, in force 2014)
Convention between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (1986)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1992, c. C-30; Special Economic Measures Act, R.S.C. 1992, c. C-60; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (significant control provisions, arts. 21.0.1 et seq.); Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2266 (limited partnership formation); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. No partnership-level FINTRAC reporting-entity license is required for retail sale via internet; Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe each maintain FINTRAC-compliant AML/ATF programs for the payment rails.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document of each general partner and each individual with significant control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the UBO's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if applicable) or Consular Legalization, with notarized translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency or equivalent evidence of legal existence for any corporate general or limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or Companies House of the foreign partner's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract of constitutional documents (articles/certificate of incorporation, bylaws, shareholder register) and board resolution authorizing participation in the Quebec limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary in the foreign partner's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing a Quebec representative to sign the declaration of registration and receive service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or equivalent authorized legal authority in the foreign grantor's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct mandatory enhanced due diligence on all general partners, limited partners holding directly or indirectly at least 25% participation, and all UBOs. Screen against domestic and foreign PEP lists under PCMLTFA and FATF standards, the OFAC SDN List, the UN Consolidated List, and Canadian sanctions regulations under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act. Screen by full legal name, aliases, date of birth, jurisdiction, passport number, and residential address. Re-run at onboarding and on an ongoing 90-day cycle; document all hits or negative findings in a written AML/CFT risk file maintained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Registre des entreprises / Portail de declaration en ligne (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, the official enterprise name must be in French or contain a compulsory French generic. A Quebec limited partnership must include 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' as the legal form. Non-French brand tokens are permitted only with an accepted French generic and must be presented in Latin transliteration where the original brand uses a non-Latin script; the REQ name-clearance review also requires distinctive French wording and avoids English legal-form tokens such as 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name may be renewed by filing a fresh REQ request before expiry if no conflicting right has intervened. Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 30 days of the refusal notice, including the statutory basis, any required French generic form, and a proposed modified name. If reconsideration is refused, file an administrative or judicial review application before the Court of Quebec within the statutory delay set out in CQLR c P-44.1, or alternatively submit a new name reservation with a different distinctive token; foreign applicants must act through counsel holding an apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only where it constitutes a real leased physical office in Quebec at which the limited partnership maintains premises and can receive service of process; a mere mail-drop or remote virtual address without physical presence and records is not acceptable for registration or GST/QST purposes. A serviced office or business-centre address may be used initially, provided the general partner maintains operational records accessible at the declared establishment and the REQ declaration identifies the actual principal establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. Estimated quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection is approximately 10-15% over the first three years for a low-risk DTC e-commerce business using standard payment rails. The likelihood rises to approximately 25-30% if the LP uses only a virtual office without demonstrable commercial substance, receives consumer complaints on French-language obligations, or exhibits UBO, PEP, or sanctions diligence red flags.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CCQ), Book 4, Title 'Des sociétés', Articles 2236-2241 (société en commandite) and Article 2236 (general partner liability); read with the Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises (chapter R-11.1), ss. 19-22, 25-38 (déclaration d'immatriculation) and the Regulation respecting the Registraire des entreprises (R.E.J. 1999-048).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration for a limited partnership) – prescribed form under the Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises, chapter R-11.1, s. 19.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital requirement for a limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec. Contributions are freely determined by the limited partnership agreement; no escrow account rule applies at provincial formation. The declaration must state the general partner's name and domicile and the address of the partnership's establishment. All filings require payment of the Registraire's prescribed fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the General Partner of the proposed limited partnership hereby (1) approves the formation of the limited partnership under Articles 2236 et seq. of the Civil Code of Quebec; (2) subscribes to the limited partnership units as set forth in the partnership agreement; (3) adopts the partnership agreement in its final form; (4) designates the registered office and address for service at [Address], [City], Quebec [Postal Code]; (5) appoints [Name] as President and [Name] as Secretary; and (6) authorizes the executing officers to sign and file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve and clear the proposed limited partnership name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online name search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ website's 'Recherche d'un nom' tool. Input the proposed name and confirm that the exact name is not used by a legal person or partnership in the REQ central register. Ensure the name includes the legal suffix 'Société en commandite' (French) or 'Limited Partnership' (English) as required under the Civil Code of Quebec, art. 2236 and the Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises, art. 5. If the name is available, proceed to the next step. Optionally, record a name reservation request via the 'Avis de constitution' form to hold the name for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed name in French or English with appropriate suffix
List of general and limited partners
Identification of the general partner (passport or driver's licence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion with an existing name, file a new application for a distinct alternate name or request a written justification from the REQ pursuant to the Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises, s. 4.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal governance – not a government filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement under Articles 2236-2241 CCQ. The agreement must set out the name, establishment address, object, contributions of each partner (amount and form), share of profits and losses, management rights of the general partner, and dissolution events. Sign and date the agreement before a notary or by counterparts; notarization is not required for formation but recommended for real property contributions. Keep the original in the partnership file.
required_dossiers: Text of the limited partnership agreement
Identification of each partner (passport or driver's licence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is incomplete, the partners may amend by supplementary deed; the REQ declaration must reflect the final terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Declaration of Registration to REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online 'Déclaration d'immatriculation' portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the REQ's secure portal (or submit the paper form) and complete the Declaration of Registration (form RE-001). Include the establishment address in Quebec, the name and address of every general partner (natural person or legal entity with its own REQ registration), the object of the enterprise, and the date the enterprise commences. Pay the prescribed registration fee (approximately CAD 50) using credit card or interac. Upon filing, the REQ will issue a notification of inscription and assign a NEQ number.
required_dossiers: Proof of establishment address (lease or utility bill)
Identification of the general partner (name, address, date of birth and citizenship if natural person; or REQ registration number if legal person)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of non-compliance or queries a missing timestamp or partner, the general partner may file a corrective declaration within 90 days; if the deadline passes, the registration is deemed null, requiring a new registration and payment of an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax accounts with Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the NEQ, log in to Revenu Québec and apply for the GST/QST registration, the source deductions account (if staff are planned), and the QST account. Revenu Québec will issue an account number and a confirmation notice valid for both provincial and federal sales tax. GST/QST registration is mandatory if taxable total sales exceed CAD 30,000 per calendar year.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused or delayed, call Revenu Québec's business line (1-800-567-4692) and provide the request acknowledgement; a correction may be filed through the 'Opérations sur le dossier' tab.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure municipal business licence and zoning compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal or Ville de Québec) – licensing and permits division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Visit the municipality's licensing service and apply for the 'licence d'entreprise'. Provide the NEQ, the establishment address, the nature of the activity (ISC code), and a lease or proof of ownership. The municipality will verify the immobility zoning (commercial district) and issue a 'certificat d'occupation' (occupancy permit) for the retail facility. If the business operates solely from home (e-commerce), a home business permit may be required; if the DTC brand has a warehouse, a specific 'occupancy permit' is mandatory.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning is refused, file for a 'dérogation mineure' before the municipal 'Comité consultatif d'urbanisme' or relocate to a permitted zone.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 online retail; no provincial industrial authority mandates a licence. If the brand later operates a physical production or a large warehouse, the competent authority is the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) for industrial permits, and the local municipality for business licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no provincial or federal industrial operating licence is required for a pure online retail activity. A municipal 'licence d'entreprise' and, if applicable, a warehouse occupancy permit are the only mandatory permits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is listed as no EIA required under the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment and review (chapter Q-2, r. 23).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For office/warehouse operations: comply with municipal wastewater bylaws and Quebec's Clean Water Regulation; emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from packing materials remain below the CEPA threshold of 100 kg/year; shipping and receiving operations must not create disturbing noise beyond 45 dB at the nearest residential limit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The building must meet the Quebec Construction Code (chapter B-1.1) and the fire safety chapter of the Code de sécurité. A fire safety certificate is required from the Direction de la prévention en sécurité incendie. For any commercial space, a structural load clearance (including snow loading for Quebec) from an engineer is a prerequisite; CNESST's occupational health and safety clearance for office and warehouse must be filed within 3 days of hiring staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business/register.html); Revenu Québec (RQ) – Clic Revenu / Mon dossier d'entreprise portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/); Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca for the NEQ (Québec enterprise number).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Limited Partnership with REQ under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and Civil Code of Québec arts. 2236–2246 to obtain the 10-digit NEQ; file the declaration of registration identifying general/limited partners and the registered office (2–5 business days). Step 2: Use the NEQ to open a CRA Business Number (BN) via BRO and activate the GST/HST account (program code RT0001) once worldwide taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 in any single calendar quarter or over the trailing four calendar quarters (ETA small-supplier test); register within 60 days of becoming a registrant. Step 3: After the BN is issued, apply for the QST account with Revenu Québec using the same NEQ and CRA confirmation; the QST small-supplier threshold is also C$30,000. Step 4: File the combined GST/HST and QST returns through Revenu Québec's portal (Quebec filers) or CRA NETFILE as applicable, on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis, with the registration effective from the first taxable supply date; retain the BN/QST registration certificates for foreign bank and PSP onboarding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in Canada; tax classification is statutory. A Canadian LP is fiscally transparent for income tax (ITA s. 96) and is a separate registrant person for GST/HST and QST. Relevant elections: (i) ITA s. 97(2) election to transfer property to the partnership on a tax-deferred rollover basis; (ii) ETA s. 273 GST/HST joint venture election, mirrored by the QST regime, allowing a designated operator to report and remit for a qualifying joint venture; (iii) election to align the partnership's reporting period and GST/HST-QST filing frequency with CRA/RQ approvals; (iv) Canada's hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 12.7, 12.8, 18.5, 18.6) apply automatically, with only limited regulatory elections for securitization entities and no elective check-the-box for non-resident investors.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (federal GST/HST at 5% plus Quebec QST at 9.975%, layered multi-stage value-added tax; combined headline rate 14.975%, administered federally by the CRA and in Quebec by Revenu Québec under the Canada-Quebec tax administration coordination agreement)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 CAD (small supplier threshold; based on worldwide taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies, of the partnership and associated entities in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters and the current quarter; registration for both GST/HST and QST is mandatory within 60 days of exceeding the threshold; the simplified mandatory registration regime for non-resident digital-service suppliers effective July 1, 2021 has no threshold but is not applicable to this domestic Quebec LP)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority digital stamping, or per-invoice pre-approval exists in Canada or Quebec for B2C e-commerce. Quebec imposes a mandatory B2B electronic invoicing duty on large supply chains (enterprises with operating revenue of C$50M or more must issue and receive e-invoices under Revenu Québec rules), which is not binding on this Shopify DTC seller. Voluntary PEPPOL interoperability is available. Mandatory electronic reporting applies through CRA GST/HST NETFILE and Revenu Québec's Clic Revenu portal; Shopify transaction data (order, payment, fulfillment, tax export logs) must be retained for 6 years as the evidentiary base for nexus and rate application, but no government clearance API or stamping is triggered.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V when supplied by sale from Canada to a destination outside Canada, exported in a commercially reasonable time (CRA guidance normally expects export as soon as circumstances permit and ordinarily within 60 days of delivery), and not used or consumed in Canada before export; DTC parcel shipments by mail or courier to foreign customer addresses qualify. Services: ancillary digital and platform services supplied to non-residents (e.g., app subscriptions, digital marketing, order-processing services) are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V where the recipient is a non-resident and the service does not relate to real property or tangible personal property located in Canada; QST zero-rating rules are substantively identical. Sales to Canadian-resident consumers remain taxable at 14.975%; the zero-rate is claimed on the GST/HST-QST return and is supported by the export-evidence bundle retained in the Shopify order record.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: CBSA B13A Export Declaration (Canada Customs Coding Form) for shipments exceeding C$2,000; for low-value DTC parcels, the Canada Post/courier customs manifest, CBSA-accepted parcel export report, or carrier-generated export declaration capturing export date, destination country, shipment value, and customs exit scan; Shopify fulfillment export records cross-referenced.

Bill of Lading / Airway Bill: through bill of lading, courier air waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing shipment from a Canadian point of export to the foreign delivery address, including carrier tracking history with foreign customs entry scan and delivery confirmation.

Inward Remittance / Payment Evidence: bank statements and settlement reports from Shopify Payments, Stripe, or PayPal evidencing receipt of foreign-currency funds and CAD conversion, cross-referenced to order ID, payment transaction ID, and customs declaration (practical Canadian adaptation of the Inward Remittance Certificate standard).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal four-year limitation period, with no expiry where misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, willful default, or fraud exists. Unsubstantiated zero-rating is reversed on assessment: the full 14.975% GST/HST-QST becomes payable with prescribed interest compounded daily. Additional penalties include: (i) up to 25% of net tax for gross negligence under ETA s. 280 and the corresponding Quebec penalty provisions; (ii) failure-to-register penalties and false-statement penalties under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Tax Administration Act; (iii) criminal sanctions for willful evasion under ETA ss. 327–331; (iv) retrospective ITC clawback where exported goods are diverted to domestic use or where zero-rating documentation is fabricated; DTC exporters must retain the full export-evidence bundle for at least six years and respond to CRA/RQ 'export evidence' audit requests with order-level traceability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary and financial system authority; day-to-day FX administration is not centralized in a dedicated exchange-control ministry. Regulatory oversight of payments, clearing, and settlement systems is shared between the Bank of Canada, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full and unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital account transactions; there are no exchange controls, no prior authorization requirements for foreign investment in a Quebec Limited Partnership (LP), and no restrictions on profit remittances or repatriation of capital. For a Canadian-domiciled LP with non-resident partners, distributions of Canadian-source income are generally not subject to Canadian withholding tax when paid to non-residents of Canada, provided the income is characterized as partnership business income and not as Part XIII withholding-tax-eligible items (e.g., management fees, interest, or royalties separately invoiced); however, non-resident partners earning Canadian-source business income may become subject to Canadian income tax filings under Section 150 of the Income Tax Act. DTC e-commerce sales via Shopify are treated as ordinary active business income, and conversion of foreign-currency settlement balances (USD/EUR) into CAD is freely permitted at any authorized bank or fintech. Practical remittance hurdles are limited to: (i) bank compliance with FATCA/CRS reporting for non-resident beneficial owners; (ii) Quebec's commercial registry transparency for ultimate beneficial owners; and (iii) potential Canadian GST/QST registration obligations for online sales, none of which restrict currency convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement in Canada; exporters and online sellers are not obligated to repatriate or convert export proceeds within a prescribed timeline, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio. Under the Currency Act and Bank of Canada Act, the Canadian dollar shall be used as legal tender, but settlement in foreign currency is freely negotiable. For accounting and tax purposes, an accrual-basis Quebec LP must report foreign-currency gains and losses under subsection 39(1.1) of the Income Tax Act and must translate foreign-currency balances using the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate for income tax filing; however, no remittance deadline applies to the underlying funds. For robust treasury practice, the LP should proactively sweep USD settlement balances into CAD within 1-3 business days using a bank FX forward or spot order to mitigate currency depreciation risk; this is a policy choice, not a statutory mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD multi-currency) plus Capital Escrow Account if required by third-party lenders

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD) for Quebec-domiciled entities; strong regional compliance familiarity with Quebec LP structures
Operational Account with cross-border USD clearing; Capital Escrow Account capable
Operational Account; USD clearing via TD Bank US
Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account capable

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for settlement/fintech payment operations; Low as a replacement for regulated banking infrastructure. Canada does not issue a dedicated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) license; cross-border fintechs such as Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA and, for Quebec, must also hold a money-services business license from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) under the Money-Services Businesses Act (Québec, chapter M-30.1). For a Shopify DTC brand, such platforms are viable for (i) receiving payouts from marketplace clearing, (ii) converting USD/EUR retail proceeds into CAD, and (iii) disbursing supplier payments at lower cost. Primary legal constraints: (a) MSBs are prohibited from providing true deposit-taking or checking-account services, so all settlement balances must ultimately be swept to a Schedule I bank account; (b) Quebec licensing adds approval lead time; (c) MSBs cannot issue documentary letters of credit or provide credit facilities; and (d) significant counterparty concentration and platform risk limits their use for capital escrow or treasury reserves. Recommended arrangement: operate a Schedule I bank account as the treasury anchor and use a single FINTRAC/AMF-licensed MSB only as a payment platform pass-through.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banking law does not impose a statutory requirement that directors or partners appear physically; however, in practice, most Schedule I Canadian banks mandate either (i) an in-person identity verification of the general partner's authorized signatories or (ii) remote video verification coupled with notarized documents and a corporate registry extract. Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC guidance, a Canadian bank must verify the identity of: (1) the Quebec Limited Partnership itself using the official extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); (2) the general partner and its authorized signatories; and (3) every beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the partnership. Remote opening is permissible if the bank's internal KYC policy accepts electronic identification (e.g., government-issued ID with document verification technology and a contemporaneous video call), but the LP must provide the partnership agreement, certificate of declaration (Declaration of Limited Partnership), Quebec TP-600 tax registration or a demonstration of registration status, and a detailed source-of-funds narrative for planned Shopify settlement flows. A physical meeting or an in-branch notarized signing may be accelerated for the National Bank of Canada and Desjardins branches located in Montreal or Quebec City; RBC, TD, BMO, and CIBC generally permit assisted video onboarding for low-risk e-commerce retailers but subject to Corporate/Commercial risk committee review for partnerships with non-resident partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: QuebEC LP with multiple non-resident limited partners, where the identity of underlying 25%+ interest holders is not readily visible on the REQ registry, or where the general partner is itself a foreign corporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Current REQ attestation showing the LP's registration number and general partner; (2) full, executed partnership agreement listing each limited partner's legal name, jurisdiction, percentage interest, and capital contribution; (3) Beneficial Ownership Register of the LP prepared in compliance with the Canada Business Corporations Act equivalent and Quebec's transparency requirements, confirming ultimate natural persons (even if not individually named on REQ); (4) organizational chart flowing from the LP through the GP to the ultimate parent; (5) government-issued IDs and proof of address of each beneficial owner; (6) certified corporate certificates of incumbency for corporate partners

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, externally sourced digital retail payment flows from Shopify/PayPal/Stripe that complicate source-of-funds validation and may look like 'collection accounts' or transaction laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed Shopify Merchant Agreement and payment-processing contracts with Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe; (2) historical monthly payout statements (bank-level export) demonstrating a consistent DTC commerce pattern; (3) website URL and product catalog evidencing bona fide retail activity; (4) customer order data summary showing average ticket size and refund/chargeback ratio under 1%; (5) rationale of settlement currency conversions; (6) assurance that the account will not be used to accept funds from unrelated third parties

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from foreign jurisdictions with perceived high AML risk or from a related non-resident parent company, potentially raising expections of tax evasion or undocumented loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Board/GP resolution authorizing the capital contribution and designating the purpose ('working capital for DTC e-commerce expansion'); (2) source-of-wealth statement for the contributing partner (bank reference letter, audited financial statements, or tax returns); (3) executed subscription or contribution agreement; (4) proof of underlying transaction (e.g., sale of equity, dividend declaration) from the paying entity; (5) CRS/FATCA self-certification forms of the contributing entity; (6) projected 12-month cash-flow forecast demonstrating business purpose

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the low-risk e-commerce profile and proposed transaction volume (e.g., sudden large supplier disbursements in USD or EUR without prior history)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Supplier proforma invoices, purchase orders, and shipment contracts; (2) logistics contract (2PL/3PL) identifying the fulfillment warehouse; (3) inventory purchase plan and merchant account payout reconciliation; (4) executed LC instruction or SWIFT MT103 templates; (5) trade compliance declarations and import documentation for Canada Border Services Agency; (6) updated cash-flow forecast and board-approved treasury policy

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital contributions from a non-resident limited partner into the Quebec LP's bank account shall be routed via SWIFT MT103 through a Canadian Schedule I bank's correspondent network, with the following protocols: (i) the remitter must clearly state the purpose code and reference 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - CA_LP - ISIC 4791 DTC E-COMMERCE' to ensure the depository bank does not classify the inflow as a loan; (ii) the receiving bank's compliance intake must receive a copy of the executed subscription/contribution agreement, the LP's REQ registration extract, and the partner's FATCA/CRS self-certification before or at the time of the wire; (iii) the principal currency should be CAD but USD inward wires are acceptable, to be immediately converted to CAD via a documented spot contract to eliminate open exposure; (iv) for transactions above CAD 100,000, the general partner must provide an executed board resolution and a source-of-wealth summary; (v) inter-company repayments or advances are discouraged unless textually labelled as inter-company loans with a clear term sheet and are subject to section 17(1) of the Income Tax Act for deemed interest; (vi) the LP must also evidence the capital contribution in its inter-entity capital account and reflect it in the annual financial statements for audit trail cleanliness.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the Shopify DTC brand operational model, outbound trade disbursements shall be executed through the following clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-US international suppliers (factories in China, Vietnam, or Europe), using standard trade settlement instructions with a bank draft; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) as an optional instrument when the supplier demands payment security for large purchase orders above USD 250,000, but for the initial low-risk profile, TT (telegraphic transfer) prepayment is preferred to avoid L/C costs; (iii) Automated Clearing House (ACH) and Fedwire for US-based suppliers and 3PL partners, executed from the USD sweep account at the Schedule I bank; (iv) Shopify's own payout rails (direct deposit to the LP's CAD account) for settlement from Shopify Payments, with a controlled pool structure ensuring that Shopify, PayPal, and Stripe each settle directly into the LP's single treasury account rather than a third-party aggregation account; (v) Interac e-Transfer is permitted only for petty cash/expense reimbursement and shall never be used for supplier trade settlements; (vi) the Shopify payment provider disbursements must be funded by the merchant's own account logic; all outbound wires require dual-signature authorization (GP signatory plus an unrelated officer) above CAD 10,000 per transaction; and (vii) each wire must include the corresponding purchase order or supplier invoice number, to be retained in the trade settlement register for the statutory books of the LP.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter (OTC) FX forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank for USD/CAD and EUR/CAD risk, subject to an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA credit support annex if required

FX swaps (swap-out and swap-in) transacted for near-term settlement liquidity requirements, permitted under Canadian commodities and derivatives legislation without OSFI authorization when executed through a regulated bank as principal

Cross-currency swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for hedging the currency and interest rate exposure of any future supplier financing or inter-company loan, though likely unnecessary at the initial treasury stage

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible in Canada but are not operationally required for fully convertible CAD; they would be used only for exotic currency pairs (e.g., CNY/INR) and should be avoided during the first year of operations

FX currency options (plain vanilla European-style calls and puts) are permissible for hedging unexpected currency volatility and provide downside protection without obligating the LP to transact at an unfavourable rate, requiring a board-approved treasury policy documenting the hedge rationale and maximum notional

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updating declaration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally between June 15 and September 15 each year for a registered partnership; confirm the entity-specific deadline in the Québec Enterprise Register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Indexed annual registration fees, late charges, administrative enforcement, and potential cancellation of registration after statutory notices and continued non-compliance; cancellation is not ordinarily triggered by one isolated late filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership and enterprise-register information confirmation or amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirm through the annual updating declaration and file amendments generally within 30 days after a reportable change, including changes to ultimate beneficiaries, partners, control, or registered information.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties, filing rejection or compliance notices, and potential cancellation of registration for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (Form T5013) and related information slips, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within five months after the end of the partnership fiscal period; information slips are generally due by the last day of the third month following the partnership year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties generally calculated on a daily basis, subject to statutory minimums and maximums; additional penalties may apply for missing, inaccurate, or unissued information slips.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec Partnership Information Return (Form TP-600) and related RL-15 information slips, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within five months after the end of the partnership fiscal period; RL-15 slips generally follow the prescribed Québec information-slip deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest and late-filing or information-reporting penalties may apply; the return does not itself cause corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general Québec or Canadian statutory independent-audit threshold applies solely because the entity is a private limited partnership conducting ordinary e-commerce. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, financing documents, investor requirements, securities rules, or a regulated activity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No single statutory financial-statement framework is universally mandatory for a private Québec limited partnership. Accounting records should generally follow Canadian ASPE for private enterprises or IFRS where elected or required, subject to the partnership agreement and tax-reporting requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Confirm and update Québec Enterprise Register information annually and within the prescribed change-reporting period. Review all partners, control rights, ownership interests, and ultimate beneficiaries after each transfer or governance change. A shareholding transfer is not effective for compliance purposes until the applicable partner and beneficial-ownership records are updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes or Written Resolutions of Partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 500-1,500 annually for professional registered-office, correspondence, and corporate-administration services; Québec does not generally require a separate resident agent equivalent to a U.S. registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,500-8,000 for a basic independent audit of a small private partnership; no audit cost applies where no audit is contractually or legally required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined top general corporate rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); the Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and not a taxable entity, so this rate applies only to corporate partners on Canadian-source income allocated from the LP.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Corporate partners eligible for the federal Small Business Deduction (reduced rate 9% on first C$500,000 of active business income) and the Quebec small business rate reduction; SR&ED tax credits and Quebec innovation/credits may also lower effective tax on eligible Canadian development activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return filed with CRA via EFILE or My Business Account (Internet File Transfer); Quebec: Revenu Québec CO-5013 Partnership Information Return and related RL slips filed through Revenu Québec's CLICK portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end; for a December 31 fiscal period-end, the federal and Quebec deadlines are May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the Limited Partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the LP's fiscal period-end; non-resident limited partners must receive this date on their T5013/RL slips and report Canadian-source business income accordingly.
Quote the LP's federal business number and Quebec QST account; non-resident partners need this number for treaty relief claims and for tax clearance certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net income/loss to each partner, including each partner's share percentage
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the share allocated to each non-resident partner; if the non-resident provides a TRC, the allocation forms the basis for Part I taxation or treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payments made to non-arm's length non-resident persons (management fees, royalties, interest, platform service fees)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border payments; these amounts may be subject to Part XIII withholding and transfer pricing review by CRA/Revenu Québec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CRA late-filing penalty: C$25 per partner per day, minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500; additional gross negligence penalty may apply. Revenu Québec late penalty: 5% of the amount not declared plus 1% per month for up to 12 months.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec: RL-15 slip for partnership income and Revenu Québec CO-5013 information return (where required) filed via Revenu Québec CLICK electronic services.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the Quebec fiscal period-end (harmonized with federal; for December 31 year-ends, deadline is May 31 of the next year; no extension for non-resident partners without Canadian filings).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec fiscal period start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident limited partner, only indicate income attributable to a Quebec permanent establishment or business carried on in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenu Québec partnership registration number (NR file)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should reference the QST/NR registration number; where no Quebec permanent establishment exists, state N/A and document the position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total partnership gross revenue and expenses (including Shopify platform fees, payment processor fees, inventory costs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure gross revenue includes all Quebec-resident customer sales; QST registration may not be required for a non-resident without a Quebec permanent establishment, but all such facts must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of Quebec taxable income to each non-resident partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty relief is sought, use the allocated Quebec income as the numerator and provide a completed TRC; Revenu Québec may deny relief if allocation methodology is inconsistent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failing to file a Revenu Québec partnership return: 5% of the tax payable shown, plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated non-filing may be subject to C$250–C$10,000 provincial fines plus criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII on dividends paid by a Canadian taxable corporation; not applicable to Limited Partnership profit distributions because the LP is fiscally transparent. Remittances of a non-resident partner's share of LP income are generally treated as business income taxable under Part I, not as dividend withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a lower treaty withholding rate at source, the non-resident partner must complete and submit CRA Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Treaty) to the Canadian payor. For refund of excess withholding after year-end, file Form NR7-R. The Canadian competent authority or the foreign tax authority may require a Certificate of Residence (TRC) before granting relief; for Canada–US treaty, submit IRS Form 6166 or CRA Form RC394A where requested.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding under Part XIII: 25% on interest (unless arm's-length) and 25% on royalties paid to non-residents. Under the Canada–US treaty, arm's-length interest is generally exempt (0%); royalties for copyright, literary, artistic, or scientific works may be 0%, other IP royalties 10%. For other DTAs, rates typically range 10%–15% for royalties and 0%–15% for interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate non-arm's-length cross-border transactions during the fiscal period generally triggers CRA contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (IC 87-2R); a CAD 5,000,000 threshold applies where the partnership's total gross revenue is below CAD 50 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate ESR regime, but the general anti-avoidance rule (s.245 ITA) and Quebec's GAAR invalidate transactions lacking commercial substance. For a Limited Partnership, the limited partner's at-risk rules may disallow losses where the LP lacks economic substance; the CRA and Revenu Québec can recharacterize a sham partnership and impose penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting Shopify DTC webstore gross revenue, recording fictitious returns, using personal PayPal/Stripe accounts for commercial sales, or misrepresenting the non-resident status of the limited partner to avoid Canadian reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239(1): fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax evaded, plus imprisonment for up to 2 years; Quebec Taxation Act and Tax Administration Act impose parallel provincial fines and imprisonment; repeated anti-money-laundering breaches may trigger FINTRAC penalty up to C$500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate general partner who knowingly participate in or authorize the false reporting are jointly and severally liable for penalties; courts may pierce the LP veil under Quebec Civil Code and Canadian jurisprudence in fraud cases, ordering civil restitution, seizure of personal assets, and adverse findings preventing travel abroad if an arrest warrant is issued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File / Shell Company Abuses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file T5013 and Revenu Québec CO-5013 returns, failing to register for GST/QST once thresholds are exceeded, or using a shell non-resident limited partner with no capital contribution to shift income into a tax haven without commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA late-filing penalty up to C$2,500 per T5013, gross negligence penalty of 50% of additional tax payable, and interest; Revenu Québec penalty of 5% on the amount required plus 1% monthly; GST/QST failure to register carries penalties of 5% plus 10% of unremitted QST in some cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are jointly and severally liable for GST/QST and source deductions under Excise Tax Act s.323 and Quebec QST Act; a unilateral tax debt can become personal through solvency director's liability assessments, and directors may face travel bans while an enforcement warrant is outstanding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management fees, platform licensing fees, or interest to a non-resident related party without sufficient economic substance or contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation; also failing to withhold Part XIII on non-arm's-length royalties paid to foreign affiliated entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.247(2) transfer-pricing reassessment and s.247(3) penalty of 10% of the net adjustment (minimum C$5,000); interest compounded daily; Quebec Taxation Act applies a similar penalty. Failure to withhold Part XIII tax results in liability for the full 25% plus penalties under s.227(8) and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate general partner directors who cause the LP to pay such fees may be de facto jointly liable for Part XIII and GST/QST remittances; in egregious sham cases, personal liability extends to the full amount of unreported income, and criminal prosecution can lead to extradition requests and travel restrictions.
